claim: For the correction dynamics in Liao (2025), let \(F\) be a finite factor set with \(n=|F|\ge 2\), positive maximal grades \(d_m\), and let \(x^{q+1}=g(x^q)\) be Definition 4.2 with \(0<\alpha<2/n\). Because the correction added to \(x_{m,k}\) is independent of the grade \(k\) of a fixed factor \(m\), every difference \(x^q_{m,k}-x^q_{m,d_m}\) is invariant in \(q\). Combining this invariant with Theorem 4.4 gives the exact limit \(x^q_{m,k}\to \Psi_{m,d_m}+[x^0_{m,k}-x^0_{m,d_m}]\). Hence the full vector converges to the EAIE \(\Psi\) if and only if \(x^0_{m,k}-x^0_{m,d_m}=\Psi_{m,k}-\Psi_{m,d_m}\) for every positive grade. PCOMR does not enforce this condition: for \(F=\{1,2\}\), \((d_1,d_2)=(2,1)\), characteristic values \(H(0,0)=H(1,0)=H(2,0)=H(0,1)=H(2,1)=0\), \(H(1,1)=1\), and initial payoff \((x_{1,1},x_{1,2},x_{2,1})=(1,0,0)\), PCOMR holds and \(\Psi=(0,0,0)\), yet every correction is zero and \(x^q=x^0\) for all \(q\). Therefore Theorem 4.5 is false as written; under PCOMR it becomes valid precisely when the additional compatibility identities \(H(d_{-m},k)-H(d)=\Psi_{m,k}-\Psi_{m,d_m}\) hold for all \(m,k\).
integrity: The primary source's Definition 4.2, Theorems 4.4-4.5, PCOMR definition, and algorithm were read in the open publisher PDF and checked against page images.
The minimal counterexample and the structural grade-gap invariant are reproduced by exact rational arithmetic in verify.py.
A 2021 full-text multichoice dynamic predecessor was inspected to compare the grade dependence of its correction map.
scientific_limitations: The result concerns the full-vector convergence statement in Theorem 4.5 and the associated iteration; it does not challenge the top-grade convergence theorem.
PCOMR initializations satisfying the stated compatibility identities do converge to the full EAIE; the obstruction is not universal failure of the iteration.
The 2012 duplicate-EANSC dynamic paper was located only at abstract/bibliographic level during this run.
title: Within-factor grade gaps obstruct full convergence of the EAIE correction dynamics
